panel.empty: No providers enabled. Enable providers in Settings.

settings.title: Model Usage Settings
settings.description: Configure how usage appears in the bar, how providers are refreshed, and which providers are enabled or visible.

overview.label: Overview
overview.desc: Quick summary of the current configuration before you adjust the details below.

general.label: General
general.desc: These settings control the overall behavior of the bar widget and how provider data is refreshed.

barDisplay.label: Bar display
barDisplay.desc: Choose what the bar shows and how it behaves when multiple providers are available.

cycle.label: Cycle through providers
cycle.desc: When enabled, the bar shows one provider at a time and rotates through them. When disabled, all visible providers are shown together in the bar.
cycle.intervalDesc: How often the bar moves to the next provider while cycling is enabled.

barMetric.label: Bar metric
barMetric.desc: Choose the number or percentage shown next to each provider in the bar.

hover.label: Show text on hover
hover.desc: When enabled, the bar defaults to icons and reveals the metric text when you hover over the widget. This is useful when you want a more compact bar.

usageDisplay.label: Usage display
usageDisplay.desc: These options are most relevant when the selected bar metric shows a usage percentage, but icon alerts can still be configured here at any time.
usageDisplay.nonUsage: You are currently showing a non-usage bar metric, so the remaining-percentage option will not affect the bar right now.
usageDisplay.remainingDesc: Switches usage metrics from consumed percentage to remaining percentage. For example, 80% used becomes 20% remaining.

iconAlert.label: Color icon red on rate limit reached
iconAlert.desc: Highlights provider icons when their usage crosses the alert threshold. This makes approaching limits easier to notice in the bar at a glance.
iconAlert.windowDesc: Off uses the 7d usage window. On uses the 5h usage window. Providers without the selected window will not alert.
iconAlert.thresholdDescEnabled: The selected window's used percentage at which the provider icon switches to the warning color.
iconAlert.thresholdDescDisabled: This threshold is saved now and will take effect when icon alerts are enabled.

refresh.label: Refresh behavior
refresh.desc: Control how often local files are polled and how frequently API-backed providers are refreshed.
refresh.cacheLabel: Include cache tokens in token count
refresh.cacheDesc: Counts cache read and cache write tokens in totals wherever the provider exposes them. Disable this if you want to focus only on direct input and output tokens.
refresh.intervalDesc: Fallback polling interval for local file-based providers when file watching does not catch an update.
refresh.apiIntervalDesc: How often to poll API-backed providers such as Codex API mode, OpenRouter, Zen, Kilo Code, Z.ai, and Gemini.

providers.label: Providers
providers.desc: Enable providers, choose which ones appear in the bar, and configure provider-specific details when needed.
providers.orderDesc: Manual order is used directly, or as a tie-breaker when sorting by recently changed usage.
providers.recentHelp: Providers whose selected usage percentage changed most recently move to the front. Providers without that usage window stay in your manual drag order. This recent-change history resets when the shell restarts.
providers.recentLimitDesc: Limits how many visible providers can appear in the bar while recent-change sorting is enabled. The panel still shows every enabled provider.
providers.dragHelp: Drag providers to set the manual order. The manual order also acts as the tie-break order when recent-change sorting is enabled.
providers.enabledSummary: Enabled. Open details to configure provider-specific settings.
providers.disabledSummary: Disabled. Enable this provider if you want the plugin to collect and display its usage.
providers.noAdditional: This provider does not currently expose additional settings in the panel. Its usage data will follow the general display and refresh settings above.

codexbar.label: Use Codexbar CLI
codexbar.desc: Fetch usage via the codexbar CLI instead of this provider's native API path.

codex.sourceDesc: Choose whether Codex usage is read from local files or from the ChatGPT backend API.
codex.apiHelp: API mode reads from the ChatGPT backend using auth from ~/.codex/auth.json. Use this when local files are unavailable or incomplete.
codex.localHelp: Local mode reads from ~/.codex/ files such as history.jsonl and sessions. This avoids remote polling when the local data is sufficient.

apiKey.openrouterDesc: You can leave this empty if OPENROUTER_API_KEY is already set in your environment.
apiKey.openrouterPlaceholder: OPENROUTER_API_KEY env var or enter key here
apiKey.zenDesc: You can leave this empty if OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY or OPENCODE_API_KEY is already set in your environment.
apiKey.zenPlaceholder: OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY / OPENCODE_API_KEY env var or enter key here
apiKey.deepseekDesc: You can leave this empty if DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is already set in your environment.
apiKey.deepseekPlaceholder: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY env var or enter key here
apiKey.kilocodeDesc: You can leave this empty if KILO_API_KEY is set in your environment, or if you have authenticated via kilo login.
apiKey.kilocodePlaceholder: KILO_API_KEY env var or enter key here
apiKey.zaiDesc: You can leave this empty if Z_AI_API_KEY is already set in your environment.
apiKey.zaiPlaceholder: Z_AI_API_KEY env var or enter key here

settings.footerHelp: Use Reset to restore manifest defaults. Save is handled by Noctalia when you apply settings.
